reviewOutcome: The Asella municipal portal and general Ethiopian/Addis cadastral material were reachable, but no Asella-specific local registry custodian, public parcel service, safe native ID schema, CRS, or anonymous ID-plus-geometry response was verified. The packet is complete as discovery evidence and is held from runtime qualification.
queryAndRequestOutcomes: Separate English and Afaan Oromo/Amharic discovery queries were executed. GET requests to the Asella portal, its linked dashboard, the Addis e-Land map viewer, and the Ministry of Justice directive page returned HTTP 200. The Asella dashboard exposed only a client-side editorial login gate and no cadastral service. The e-Land viewer JavaScript was inspected; it was Addis Ababa-scoped and did not expose an Asella parcel response.
cityOrLocalCustodian: No Asella municipal land/cadastral custodian was established from the inspected first-party pages. Addis Ababa Land Holding Registration and Information Agency material is general/other-city evidence and was not treated as an Asella registry.
safeFieldAllowlist: stable native parcel ID when independently verified
scopeLimits: No exact-point or map-extent absence inference.
WUP point remains exactly [7.95577279468539, 39.1323285719823] in latitude/longitude order.
No credentials, private tokens, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, or TLS verification disablement was used.
No parcel owner, address, titleholder, personal, tax/account, or contact fields were requested or retained.
No registry, catalog, runtime configuration, queue, identity ledger, or global report was changed.
uncertainty: A local Oromia/Asella land office or authenticated workflow may provide parcel geometry in a future attempt. The public-source failure here is not evidence of cadastral absence.
integrationDisposition: Research packet only; no source integration or admission.
